corpus.content: Redis expiration associates a timeout with a key. Passive expiration checks the deadline when the key is accessed. Active expiration periodically samples keys with expiration deadlines and deletes expired keys. Expiration frees memory and prevents stale values from remaining available indefinitely. The TTL command reports remaining lifetime in seconds, while PTTL reports milliseconds.

PostgreSQL transactions group statements into an atomic unit. BEGIN starts a transaction, COMMIT makes its changes durable, and ROLLBACK discards its uncommitted changes. Savepoints allow rollback of part of a transaction. Other sessions observe changes according to the configured isolation level. A failed statement can leave a transaction in an aborted state until rollback.

Kafka stores records in ordered partition logs. Each record receives an offset within its partition. Records in the same partition can be consumed in offset order. Kafka does not provide a single total order across different partitions. Selecting a consistent key normally routes related records to the same partition. Consumer groups distribute partition ownership between consumers.

Elasticsearch uses an inverted index to map indexed terms to documents containing them. An analyzer converts input text into tokens during indexing and query analysis. Search combines matching term postings to find documents. Text fields are analyzed for full-text search, while keyword fields preserve exact values for filtering and aggregation. Refresh makes recent index changes visible to search.

Docker containers run isolated processes that share the host kernel. Linux namespaces isolate process IDs, mounts and network views. Control groups constrain resource usage such as CPU and memory. Image layers provide a reusable filesystem base and containers add a writable layer. Isolation depends on kernel features and configuration; a container is not a separate virtual machine kernel.

Kubernetes readiness probes determine whether a container is ready to receive service traffic. When a readiness probe fails, the pod is excluded from the relevant service endpoints. Readiness failure does not itself restart the container. Liveness probes serve a different purpose and can trigger restarts. Startup probes protect slow-starting applications from premature liveness checks.

FastAPI uses Pydantic models to validate structured request bodies. Declared field types and constraints reject invalid inputs before the route handler runs. Invalid requests normally receive an HTTP 422 response with validation details. A model can require fields, constrain numeric ranges and limit string lengths. Response models validate and serialize the handler result into the public response shape.

Nginx can act as a reverse proxy using the proxy_pass directive inside a location block. It receives the client request and forwards it to the configured upstream application. Proxy headers can preserve the original host and client address. Streaming responses require suitable buffering settings and timeouts. An upstream connection failure is distinct from an application response with an error status.

RabbitMQ consumer acknowledgements inform the broker that a delivered message has been processed. With manual acknowledgements, the consumer acknowledges a delivery after successful work. An unacknowledged message can be requeued when its channel or connection closes. Negative acknowledgements can request requeue or rejection. Publisher confirms are a separate mechanism for confirming that publishing reached the broker.

SQLite write-ahead logging records database changes in a WAL file before checkpointing them into the main database file. Readers can access a stable snapshot while a writer appends changes to the WAL. SQLite still permits only one writer at a time. Checkpointing transfers committed pages back into the database. WAL mode is enabled with PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and depends on shared access to related files.
